title: Prefix & Suffix Workshop
intro: Unclear, disagree, kindness. Pick the form of the word that fits the gap.

A2.q: The instructions were completely ___ (clear) — nobody could follow them.
A2.why: “Nobody could follow them”, so not clear: un- makes the opposite.

A2.q: She was very ___ (care) with the antique vase.
A2.why: Taking care with a vase: “careful”. “Caring” is about being kind to people.

A2.q: He felt ___ (hope) after losing his job and saw no way out.
A2.why: Losing his job and no way out: -less means without, so without hope.
After “complete” we need a noun: dark + -ness.

A2.q: There’s far too much work. It’s ___ (possible) to finish this by Friday.
A2.why: Far too much work, so it cannot be done: before p the opposite takes im-, “impossible”.

A2.q: That was a very ___ (help) thing to do.
A2.why: A good thing to do: help + -ful, full of help.

A2.q: The child was ___ (fear) of the dark.
A2.why: Afraid “of the dark”: fear + -ful. “Fearless” means not afraid.

A2.q: This bag is ___ (use) — it has a hole in it.
A2.why: A bag with a hole has no use: -less means without.
After “their” we need a noun: kind + -ness.

A2.q: It was ___ (fair) to blame her for the mistake.
A2.why: Blaming her for a mistake was not fair: un- makes the opposite.

A2.q: The cowboy was very ___ (luck) — his horse lost a shoe in the desert.
A2.why: A lost horseshoe in the desert is bad luck: un- makes the opposite of “lucky”.

A2.q: The fruit stalls at the Mercado Central are very ___ (colour): red, green, yellow and orange.
A2.why: Red, green, yellow and orange: full of colour, so colour + -ful.

B1.q: I completely ___ (agree) with that decision: I think it’s a terrible idea.
B1.why: A terrible idea means you do not agree, and the opposite of agree takes dis-: “disagree”.

B1.q: The waiter ___ (understand) my order and brought something completely different.
B1.why: He brought the wrong dish, so he understood wrongly: mis- means badly or wrongly.
After “very” we need an adjective: comfort + -able.

B1.q: He gave a clear ___ (explain) of the rules.
B1.why: After “a clear” we need a noun: explain → “explanation” (no i in the middle).

B1.q: The committee strongly ___ (approve) of the plan and voted against it.
B1.why: They voted against it, so they did not approve: “disapprove of”.
Information that gives a wrong idea: mis- + leading.

B1.q: The instructions are ___ (understand) even for beginners.
B1.why: “Even for beginners”, so easy to understand: -able means can be.

B1.q: Everything is ready, so it’s ___ (like) that the meeting will be postponed.
B1.why: Everything is ready, so a delay is not likely: un- + likely gives “unlikely”.

B1.q: The company faced ___ (satisfy) customers after the delay.
B1.why: Unhappy customers after a delay: the opposite of satisfied takes dis-.

B1.q: In the past, doctors often ___ (diagnose) the disease because the symptoms looked like flu.
B1.why: Mistaken for flu, so diagnosed wrongly: mis- means wrongly.

B1.q: The new tram line to the beach in Valencia was very ___ (success).
B1.why: After “very” we need an adjective: success + -ful.

B2.q: The government announced a new ___ (develop) plan.
B2.why: A noun before “plan”: develop + -ment, with no extra e.

B2.q: His ___ (react) to the news was unexpected.
B2.why: After “His” we need a noun: react + -ion.

B2.q: The company decided to ___ (structure) after the merger.
B2.why: Organise again after a merger: re- means again.

B2.q: She felt ___ (whelm) by the amount of work and burst into tears.
B2.why: Too much work and tears: over- means too much.

B2.q: The time needed for the project was ___ (estimate): it took twice as long as planned.
B2.why: It took twice as long as planned: the estimate was too low, so under-.
After “widespread” we need a noun: popular + -ity.

B2.q: The exam results caused a lot of ___ (anxious) among students.
B2.why: After “a lot of” we need a noun: anxious → “anxiety”.

B2.q: The council plans to ___ (modern) the town centre.
B2.why: Make something modern: -ise, the British spelling.
Put tasks in order of priority: priority → “prioritise”.

B2.q: Hand-washing led to a dramatic ___ (reduce) in deaths on Semmelweis's wards.
B2.why: After “a dramatic” we need a noun: reduce → “reduction”.

B2.q: The water at the ranch was ___ (sufficient) for so many cattle, so the cowboys moved on.
B2.why: They moved on, so not enough water: in- makes the opposite of “sufficient”.

C1.q: The scientist tried to ___ (simple) the complex theory for the public.
His argument was ___ (logic) from start to finish: none of his conclusions followed from his evidence.
C1.why: The conclusions did not follow, so it was not logical: before l the negative prefix becomes il-, “illogical”.

C1.q: The measures were designed to ___ (act) the rising crime rate.
C1.why: Measures that act against crime: counter- means against.

C1.q: Her explanation seemed rather ___ (science) — it sounded like science, but no real evidence backed it.
C1.why: It sounded like science but had no evidence: pseudo- means false.
Promises that could never come true: un- + realistic.

C1.q: It would be ___ (responsible) of me to ignore the warning.
C1.why: Before r, the negative prefix becomes ir-: “irresponsible”.

C1.q: The evidence was ___ (refute) — nobody could argue against it.
C1.why: “Nobody could argue against it”: ir- + refutable, impossible to refute.

C1.q: His resignation was met with ___ (belief) from the whole office.
C1.why: Shock at the news: the noun for not believing is “disbelief”.

C1.q: The two accounts of the accident were completely ___ (compatible).
C1.why: Two accounts that cannot both be true: in- + compatible.

C1.q: Her rise to fame was nothing short of ___ (meteor).
C1.why: A rise as fast and bright as a meteor: meteor + -ic.

C1.q: The cholera outbreak seemed ___ (explicable) until John Snow mapped the deaths around the Broad Street pump.
C1.why: A mystery until Snow’s map pointed to the cause: in- + explicable, impossible to explain.

C1.q: After the silver mine closed, the town was ___ (inhabit): not a soul remained.
C1.why: “Not a soul remained”, so nobody lived there: un- + inhabit + -ed gives “uninhabited”.
